contribution_requirements_justification:
https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md — the requirements for acceptable contributions: tests with
  every change (a bug fix includes the test that would have caught it), docs updated with the code, a CHANGELOG entry, a DECISIONS.md 
  entry for design choices, Biome lint with --error-on-warnings and TypeScript strict as the coding standard, and pnpm typecheck, lint, 
  test and docs:check must pass. CI enforces these on every pull request, and main requires them to pass.
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/blob/main/LICENSE>.
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
documentation_basics_justification: Some documentation basics file contents found.
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
repo_interim_justification:
Every change lands on main through a pull request (required by the branch ruleset), so the repository holds every interim version 
  between releases, not only releases: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/commits/main and 
  https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/pulls?q=is%3Apr. Releases are tags on main (e.g. v1.2.0).
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
version_unique_justification:
Each release has a unique semantic version number in package.json, published once to npm (npm refuses to reuse a version) and tagged in
  git, e.g. 1.2.0: https://www.npmjs.com/package/better-auth-saml-idp?activeTab=versions and 
  https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/releases
version_semver_justification:
Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with what each part promises (for users and for SPs) documented in 
  https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/blob/main/docs/guide/versioning.md
version_tags_justification:
Every release is a git tag vX.Y.Z on main, created by the tag-release workflow when the release pull request merges; the release 
  workflow refuses a tag that doesn't match package.json or isn't on main: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/tags
release_notes_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: A release that fixes a vulnerability says so in a Security section of the CHANGELOG (e.g. 1.1.3, the external review's fixes, D-065); advisories go through GitHub security advisories with CVEs where one applies (SECURITY.md)
report_process_justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/blob/main/SECURITY.md>. [osps_do_02_01]
report_responses_justification: The maintainer responds to issues; SECURITY.md sets a 7-day acknowledgement target for vulnerability reports
enhancement_responses_justification: Feature requests through the feature form; the roadmap in the README records decisions
report_archive_justification:
GitHub issues and pull requests are public, permanently archived and searchable: 
  https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-saml-idp/issues?q=is%3Aissue
build_justification: `pnpm build` (scripts/build.mjs); CI builds and packs on every change
test_justification: `pnpm test` (Vitest) on Node and on workerd with D1; documented in CONTRIBUTING
test_most_justification: About 1,500 tests on each of Node and workerd: unit, integration, SP interop, fuzzing, Playwright e2e against Keycloak and SimpleSAMLphp; the adapter matrix on Postgres, MySQL and MongoDB, including Prisma and Drizzle; the built package smoke-tested on Bun and Deno; the Next.js example built, started and signed in through on every CI run
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING: "Tests with every change. A bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it."
tests_are_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING: "Tests with every change. A bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it."
tests_documented_added_justification: Every DECISIONS entry since D-001 lists its tests; features and security fixes record mutation checks (each guard broken once and caught, e.g. D-071)
warnings_justification: TypeScript `strict`, Biome lint with `--error-on-warnings` in CI
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on lint warnings and type errors
know_secure_design_justification: docs/security.md (threat model) and docs/guide/security.md (every control); nine review rounds recorded in DECISIONS, including an external one (D-029, D-030, D-039, D-046, D-048, D-053, D-060, D-061, D-065)
know_common_errors_justification: XML signature wrapping, XXE/DOCTYPE, replay, open redirects, CSRF and injection are addressed and tested (docs/guide/security.md)
crypto_published_justification: RSA-SHA256/512 signatures, AES-GCM with RSA-OAEP encryption: published, standard algorithms (XML-DSig, XML-Enc)
crypto_call_justification: Node's crypto (OpenSSL) and xml-crypto; no custom cryptographic primitives
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography is implementable with FLOSS
crypto_keylength_justification: RSA keys of at least 2048 bits are enforced at startup; `keygen` defaults to 3072
crypto_working_justification: SHA-1 and AES-CBC are refused unless explicitly opted into (`allowInsecureSha1`, `allowInsecureCbc`), with warnings; RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 key transport isn't offered
crypto_pfs_justification: The plugin doesn't implement network protocols; TLS is the host's
crypto_password_storage_justification: The plugin stores no passwords; Better Auth does
crypto_random_justification: IDs, tokens and keys from `crypto.getRandomValues` / Node crypto
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known unpatched vulnerabilities; OSV-Scanner over every lockfile reports none (advisories without an update, all outside the published package, are recorded with reasons and an expiry in `osv-scanner.toml`)
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (security-extended) on every pull request and push to `main`, required to pass; Biome; TypeScript strict
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL alerts are fixed or dismissed with a recorded reason (D-037; on 2026-10-06 two fixed in example scripts, nine benchmark-script alerts dismissed with the reason); a pull request that adds an alert fails
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based fuzzing (fast-check) of every inbound parser and the signature verifier on every CI run; Playwright e2e in real Chromium
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: TypeScript, not a memory-unsafe language (libxml2 runs as WebAssembly, sandboxed)
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every pull request and every push to `main` (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Since D-072, `main` requires a pull request and 19 passing checks (tests on both runtimes and two Better Auth versions, the adapter matrix, e2e, CodeQL, audits, dependency review), with no bypass
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the full history in CI; test keys are generated per run
